description: Surface React components (named function / arrow / class) and hooks (`use*` convention or `@vrooliWidget` tag) as their own `NodeKind` rather than collapsing them into "function".

requirements.description: React components and hooks defined in .tsx/.jsx files must be surfaced with their own NodeKind values rather than being collapsed into the generic FUNCTION kind. A function is classified as COMPONENT if it is a named function, arrow function, or class that returns JSX and follows React component naming conventions (PascalCase). A function is classified as HOOK if its name matches the use* convention or if it carries a @vrooliWidget annotation in its leading JSDoc. This classification must be consistent with the NodeKind.COMPONENT and NodeKind.HOOK enum extensions defined in the shared proto.
requirements.title: JSX/TSX Component and Hook Declaration Awareness

validation.notes: Test that a PascalCase function returning JSX in a .tsx file is classified as COMPONENT
Test that an arrow function assigned to a PascalCase const returning JSX is classified as COMPONENT
Test that a class extending React.Component is classified as COMPONENT
Test that a function named useMyHook is classified as HOOK
Test that a function with @vrooliWidget JSDoc tag is classified as HOOK regardless of naming
Test that a utility function with camelCase name returning no JSX remains classified as FUNCTION
TCG-JSX-COMPONENT: Extract a fixture with React components and hooks; verify COMPONENT and HOOK NodeKind assignments in the graph
Verify that COMPONENT and HOOK nodes also carry correct leading_comments from their JSDoc blocks
react-component-library can query the graph for all COMPONENT and HOOK nodes without inspecting raw source files
